**Theorem 3.2.** _If the β’s returned by LearnDiscrepancy are always discrepancy functions for corresponding modes, then VerifySafety_ ( _H, U_ ) _(Algorithm 2) is sound. That is, if it outputs “SAFE”, then H is safe with respect to U and if it outputs “UNSAFE” then there exists an execution of H that enters U._

The algorithms have been implemented in DryVR and have been used to automatically verify the benchmarks from Section 2 and an Automatic Transmission System (Appendix A.2). The transition graph, the initial set, and unsafe set are given in a text file. DryVR uses simulators for modes, and outputs either “Safe” of “Unsafe”. Reachtubes or counter-examples computed during the analysis are also stored in text files.

The implementation is in Python using the MatLab’s Python API for accessing the Simulink _⃝_<sup>R</sup> simulators. Py-GLPK [31] is used to find the parameters of discrepancy functions; either global (GED) or piece-wise (PED) discrepancy can be selected by the user. Z3 [14] is used for reachtube operations. At this stage, all the benchmarks we are working on heavily rely on Mathworks _⃝_<sup>R</sup> Simulink _⃝_ R . We don’t have a public Mathworks _⃝_<sup>R</sup> license to release the tool, and it is complicated for the users to build a connection between DryVR and their own Simulink _⃝_<sup>R</sup> models. We will release DryVR soon after we move the blackbox benchmarks to a different open source software.

Figure 2 shows example plots of computed safe reachtubes and counterexamples for a simplified AutoPassing in which vehicle B stays in the cruise always. As before, vehicle A goes through a sequence of modes to overtake B. Initially, for both _i ∈{A, B}_ , _sxi_ = _vxi_ = 0 and _vyi_ = 1, i.e., both are cruising at constant speed at the center of the right lane; initial positions along the lane are _syA ∈_ [0 _,_ 2] _, syB ∈_ [15 _,_ 17]. Figure 2a shows the lateral positions ( _sxA_ in red and _sxB_ in green, in the top subplot), and the positions along the lane ( _syA_ in red and _syB_ in green, in the bottom plot).
